topic: Dynamic Batch Timeouts Cripple ML Inference Tail Latency
postText:
We enabled dynamic batching on our production model servers to push GPU utilization past 70%. In synthetic benchmarks, throughput tripled and cost dropped. Then actual clinicians logged in simultaneously across healthcare facilities.

Suddenly, critical triage predictions stalled. P99 latency exploded from 45ms to 1.2 seconds. 

The root cause was static batch timeout architecture. Dynamic batchers hold early requests in memory until `max_batch_size` fills or `max_queue_delay_microseconds` expires. Under irregular clinical traffic, early requests repeatedly waited for full timeouts. Worse, heterogeneous input sizes forced the engine to pad all tensors to the largest sequence in the batch, burning memory bandwidth on useless zeroes.

To stabilize production without buying more GPUs, we reworked the pipeline:
1. Tensor Bucketing: Ingress proxies split payloads into pre-defined shape buckets. Zero extreme padding, minimal VRAM thrashing.
2. Adaptive Queue Delays: We tied queue windows directly to ingress velocity. High velocity shrinks delay to zero; low velocity bypasses batching entirely.
3. Priority Tiering: Life-critical real-time telemetry bypasses batch queues straight to dedicated Triton instances, while asynchronous analytics soak up spare batch capacity.

Throughput without predictability is technical debt disguised as efficiency.

How do you balance GPU saturation against strict p99 SLA guarantees in your production ML stacks?
